items.prompt: Why reject a wrong-kind closer immediately?

options.text: No suffix can repair the prefix
options.why: Once a closer mismatches the current top, that prefix violates proper nesting and no later suffix can repair it.
Counts can stay balanced for ([)], yet the nesting is wrong; a negative counter is not required.
A wrong-kind closer often occurs while openers remain; being fully matched is not its cause.
Later input is not globally ignored; this particular result can return early because the first invalid prefix is already determined.

items.explanation: Proper nesting requires the current top kind.
